scope: Separate failure and platform test specifications; excluded from the 540 positive product cases.

cases.given: Yesterday recovery is carried on Today
cases.then: Suppress a current-day recovery claim; keep the dated UI value.

cases.given: Sleep session is still recording
cases.then: Wait for the finalized episode; send no completed-night recap.

cases.given: Workout score is pending Strength settlement
cases.then: Show pending state in app; delay a scored-result message.

cases.given: Current strain observation is 31 minutes old
cases.when: Target rule evaluates with a 30-minute limit
cases.then: Suppress until a current observation exists.

cases.given: Battery observation is 31 minutes old
cases.then: Reject live wording; only an eligible last-seen rule can describe it.

cases.given: Morning data arrives after the configured noon deadline
cases.then: Update the app; do not replay a morning push.

cases.given: Weekly data arrives more than 24 hours after its selected window
cases.then: Keep the report in app and expire its old scheduled notice.

cases.given: Phone is locked and the health store is unavailable
cases.then: Keep data unknown; do not interpret the failed read as a physiological change.

cases.given: User changes the active source while a candidate waits
cases.when: The coordinator is about to submit
cases.then: Revalidate source context and withdraw the old-source candidate.

cases.given: WHOOP RMSSD and Apple SDNN are present
cases.then: Compare compatible measurement types only; do not join them into one baseline.

cases.given: A workout exists from two imported sources
cases.then: Use the canonical duplicate-collapsed session identity for one result.

cases.given: Two paired straps both have low battery
cases.then: Keep device identities separate; select useful device-specific messages under the budget.

cases.given: A local sleep score and imported WHOOP score disagree
cases.then: Use the selected production source and label it; do not average the scores.

cases.given: A user-edited sleep record exists
cases.when: Historical sync sends its older boundary
cases.then: Preserve user authority and prevent an obsolete correction alert.

cases.given: The database context changes after restore
cases.then: Withdraw requests that cannot prove matching source and event ownership.

cases.given: The same stable source and event have a new database generation
cases.then: Reject stale facts but preserve the event and attention claims; generation alone is not a new occurrence.

cases.given: A recovery input is missing
cases.when: A rule needs a recovery target
cases.then: Keep the target unknown and suppress the target-based notice.

cases.given: A valid measured zero is present
cases.then: Preserve zero where the metric permits it; do not treat it as missing.

cases.given: A metric contains NaN or infinity
cases.then: Reject the value before thresholds or copy render.

cases.given: Daily strain is stored on 0 to 100 and target uses 0 to 21
cases.then: Convert once through the canonical formatter and compare one declared scale.

cases.given: Training Load has a 7/42 ratio and Readiness has a 7/28 ratio
cases.then: Use the correct named ratio and destination; never swap their labels.

cases.given: PR62 is merged but cached rows still use the old model
cases.then: Keep the dependency gate closed until repaired current data is available.

cases.given: A historical scoring migration updates 200 days
cases.then: Allow UI refresh; create no new current-event notifications from the backfill.

cases.given: No aerobic/anaerobic producer is installed
cases.when: The deferred split-load family is loaded
cases.then: Leave it disabled; do not derive the split from sport labels or HR alone.

cases.given: A wind-down for Monday sleep occurs on Sunday evening
cases.then: Use the previous weekday correctly and create one Sunday occurrence.

cases.given: DST spring transition removes a selected one-shot wall-clock minute
cases.then: Choose the first valid local time after the gap once and show the resolved time; separately test repeating OS calendar behavior on device.

cases.given: DST fall transition repeats a selected one-shot wall-clock minute
cases.then: Choose the first occurrence and one stable identifier; do not assume app code runs at each OS repeating trigger.

cases.given: The user travels to a new timezone
cases.then: Rebuild future local schedules; preserve completed event identity and budget history.

cases.given: The clock moves backward by two hours
cases.when: A scheduled slot appears due again
cases.then: Do not repeat a claimed occurrence or reset the rolling budget.

cases.given: The date changes during an active night-shift sleep
cases.then: Use the physiological wake day and completed episode; do not force a midnight recap.

cases.given: A wake time changes after a wind-down request exists
cases.then: Cancel the old revision and schedule the new correct local occurrence.

cases.given: The device reboots with reminders already pending
cases.then: Reconcile by stable identifiers; avoid adding a second set of weekday requests.

cases.given: Notification authorization is denied
cases.then: Record the reason and update in-app state without another permission prompt.

cases.given: Authorization is provisional
cases.when: A routine local request is eligible
cases.then: Respect the OS quiet-delivery state and the category choice; do not demand full authorization.

cases.given: The user has never been asked for permission
cases.then: Do not show a surprise permission prompt; request permission from a chosen foreground setup action.

cases.given: HealthKit returns no sleep samples
cases.then: Use neutral data-availability wording; do not claim read permission was denied.

cases.given: A new app version adds ten groups
cases.then: Keep new push groups off and preserve every existing choice.

cases.given: The user turns off a group during an awaited add
cases.then: Recheck the preference and remove the now-obsolete pending/delivered request where possible.

cases.given: Selected schedules exceed the 24-request management target
cases.then: Preserve accepted schedules, use generic recurring requests or a bounded one-shot horizon, and surface actual setup failure without silently dropping a chosen reminder.

cases.given: Breathe or Hydrate was never selected
cases.when: A catalog rule references that tool
cases.then: Keep its push disabled even when a related health pattern appears.

cases.given: Two callbacks contain the same evidence revision
cases.then: One transaction claims the occurrence and one budget slot.

cases.given: Durable state proves the process exited before the submitting transition and before add could run
cases.then: Revalidate and allow a still-valid initial submission; a generic reserved row with ambiguous invocation history is not enough.

cases.given: The process exits after accepted add and before ledger update
cases.then: Find the existing request and mark submitted without posting a duplicate.

cases.given: The add call fails with a known error
cases.then: Release its reservation and allow at most one retry before expiry.

cases.given: The add outcome is unknown and no pending or delivered record remains
cases.then: Record submission_uncertain and keep its attention charge; a dismissed notice may have been seen, so do not retry the proactive occurrence.

cases.given: A background task expires during evidence collection
cases.then: Cancel unfinished work and do not create a partial-data candidate.

cases.given: A new snapshot supersedes the in-flight snapshot
cases.then: Reject the stale generation and process the latest immutable facts.

cases.given: The same sleep episode is rescored with a new generation
cases.when: It still supports the same action
cases.then: Replace or update the same occurrence; do not use generation as a fresh event ID.

cases.given: Two proactive notices have been submitted today
cases.when: A third ordinary candidate becomes eligible
cases.then: Keep it in app or digest; do not exceed the daily limit.

cases.given: Ten proactive notices were submitted in the prior seven days
cases.then: Keep it out of the proactive lane until a slot ages out.

cases.given: Last proactive submission was 179 minutes ago
cases.then: Enforce the 180-minute gap; submit later only if it remains useful.

cases.given: Last proactive submission was exactly 180 minutes ago
cases.when: A valid candidate arrives and all other gates pass
cases.then: Allow its priority evaluation; do not add an off-by-one delay.

cases.given: An explicit wind-down reminder is due in 20 minutes
cases.then: Yield the proactive notice and preserve the chosen reminder.

cases.given: Sleep, recovery, and a plan conflict describe one morning
cases.when: Separate callbacks arrive before and after submission and restart
cases.then: Use the same persisted attention key so one combined morning action consumes one slot and later families cannot post again.

cases.given: Battery percentage and runtime describe the same low-charge episode
cases.when: Their rules arrive in separate callbacks after a restart
cases.then: Use the shared device-episode attention claim and submit one charge message with the best supported explanation.

cases.given: A user-requested wake alarm is due after the advice budget fills
cases.then: Preserve its existing alarm lane and do not drop it because advice slots were used.

cases.given: Private previews are enabled
cases.then: Public content contains no health value; detailed data stays in the destination.

cases.given: A journal entry contains alcohol or mood context
cases.then: Keep that sensitive context out of the public preview.

cases.given: The relevant detail screen is already visible
cases.then: Update the screen without a routine banner or sound.

cases.given: The app is active on a different screen
cases.then: Use unobtrusive in-app presentation according to category policy.

cases.given: The user disables detailed previews
cases.then: Remove exposed delivered items where supported and rebuild future generic content.

cases.given: OS Focus delays presentation beyond app expiry
cases.then: Record submitted only; do not promise presentation by expiry or automatic removal, and revalidate current status on tap.

cases.given: Apple Watch mirroring is enabled
cases.when: iOS routes a notice to the watch
cases.then: Respect system routing and do not create a second manual watch alert.

cases.given: Diagnostic logging is enabled
cases.then: Log event IDs and reason codes without raw health or journal text.

cases.given: The app is cold when a workout notice is tapped
cases.when: The route arrives before data load
cases.then: Queue the typed route and open the correct canonical workout after startup.

cases.given: The linked workout was deleted
cases.then: Show a neutral removed-record state and avoid opening a different workout.

cases.given: A notification payload has an unsupported version
cases.then: Reject unsafe fields and open a supported neutral destination.

cases.given: An active Lift session is recording
cases.then: Preserve the active session and offer review without starting or replacing exercise.

cases.given: A snooze would end after the candidate expiry
cases.then: Do not schedule stale content; show that the original reminder has expired.

cases.given: The user chooses Turn off this type
cases.then: Cancel that family only; preserve other groups and alarms.

cases.given: A Mark done action fails to save
cases.then: Keep the item incomplete and show a local error; do not consume success state.

cases.given: Onboarding or terms covers the shell
cases.then: Hold the route until the required screen completes without losing its identity.

cases.given: Battery oscillates between 14 and 15 percent
cases.then: Emit one low event; preserve the existing 25-percent rearm threshold.

cases.given: Battery is low and charging is confirmed
cases.then: Suppress the low-charge action while charging.

cases.given: The charging flag changes true to unknown at low battery
cases.then: Do not rearm solely from charging-flag changes.

cases.given: Battery reaches 25 percent after a prior low event
cases.then: Rearm the next genuine discharge episode without posting a low notice now.

cases.given: A full-charge notification exists and battery drops to 99 percent
cases.then: Remove the stale full-charge item and rearm the full event.

cases.given: Device runtime estimate is unavailable
cases.then: Do not invent remaining hours or a guaranteed failure time.

cases.given: The strap was last seen at 12 percent four hours ago
cases.then: Use last-seen time and percentage, not a claim about current charge.

cases.given: A device disconnects briefly during an ordinary reconnect
cases.then: Suppress a repair push and wait for the rule's actual persistence requirement.

cases.given: A persistent health pattern remains raised across midnight
cases.then: Keep the same episode and avoid a new warning from date rollover.

cases.given: A raised pattern is followed by unknown data
cases.then: Keep the episode unresolved; unknown must not rearm it.

cases.given: A valid clear observation follows a raised pattern
cases.when: Later valid data raises a new pattern
cases.then: Allow one new episode after the real clear transition.

cases.given: The user already logged feeling unwell
cases.when: The health engine emits its support path
cases.then: Do not describe that user report as a new detected illness.

cases.given: A sleep stage series is sparse
cases.then: Keep stage-based advice suppressed or clearly unavailable in app.

cases.given: A user corrects the sleep boundary
cases.then: Update related pending copy and dedupe by the preserved episode identity.

cases.given: A nap credit changes current Sleep Need
cases.then: Reconcile wind-down using the current plan and preserve the selected wake time.

cases.given: A forecast has a wide uncertainty band
cases.when: A user opens a planning comparison
cases.then: Show the estimate and its uncertainty in app; do not promise tomorrow's exact recovery.

cases.given: A workout summary is already open
cases.then: Refresh the result without another completion notice.

cases.given: A lift import has totals but no sets
cases.then: Describe the available contribution only; do not claim muscular-set scoring.

cases.given: Warm-up sets and working sets are both logged
cases.then: Use the established set definition and do not inflate the record.

cases.given: A scheduled workout completes before its saved reminder
cases.when: Completion is committed or observed while the app can execute
cases.then: Cancel the pending reminder and link completion to the plan; if suspended execution prevents cancellation, generic copy must remain neutral and the tap shows current completion.

cases.given: A workout is active with low heart rate during a rest interval
cases.then: Suppress routine stress prompts using explicit active-lift state.

cases.given: No water has been logged today
cases.then: Ask about logging only; do not state the person is dehydrated.

cases.given: A new journal association uses too few valid observations
cases.then: Keep it unavailable; do not present correlation as a proven cause.

cases.given: A Coach commitment was mentioned in chat but never confirmed
cases.then: Do not create a reminder until a structured user commitment exists.
